outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no new proof or counterexample to the telescope conjecture has appeared in the sources I found: the Burklund-Hahn-Levy-Schlank disproof (arXiv:2310.17459, posted 26 Oct 2023, before the frozen revision) already showed the conjectured equality fails at every height n+1 >= 2 and every prime, and since then it has been expounded (Oberwolfach and SLMath workshops, Ausoni's Bourbaki exposé, Ravenel's June 2026 companion), supported by a JAMS-published companion on cyclotomic redshift, and recognised by a Clay Research Award (14 Apr 2026), with no journal acceptance of the BHLS paper itself found and no AI system found involved.
problem_asks: (1) For each height n (n >= 1 is the content; height 0 is rationalisation, where both localisations agree) and each prime p, the telescope conjecture asserts that the natural inclusion of the K(n)-local (Bousfield/Morava) category into the T(n)-local (telescopic) category is an equality; equivalently, the finite localisation L_n^f agrees with the Bousfield localisation L_n (Barthel 2019, Conjecture 3.4: 'for any n >= 0, L_n^f -> L_n is an equivalence'). The quantifiers are universal: every prime and every height. (2) The all-heights form of the conjecture, which Barthel records as folklore-equivalent to the generalised telescope conjecture, namely that every smashing localisation of the stable homotopy category is finite. (3) The Wikipedia wording's framing, 'the last of Ravenel's conjectures in stable homotopy theory to be resolved', is a status claim (that the other Ravenel conjectures are resolved and this one is last), not a further mathematical demand; resolution in either direction would settle it. The January 2024 wording gives no explicit height or prime range; the ranges above are read from the conjecture's standard form as stated in the sources I opened.

events.what_happened: Robert Burklund, Jeremy Hahn, Ishan Levy and Tomer M. Schlank announced a disproof at the Panorama of Homotopy Theory conference in Oxford (talks 6-9 June 2023, per Ravenel's page) and posted 'K-theoretic counterexamples to Ravenel's telescope conjecture' (arXiv:2310.17459, 100 pages, math.AT and math.KT, report no. CPH-GEOTOP-DNRF151) on 26 Oct 2023; v1 is the only version listed and no journal reference is given. Abstract: 'At each prime p and height n+1 >= 2, the telescopic and chromatic localizations of spectra differ.' Theorem A, as read in the ar5iv rendering: for any prime p, n+1 >= 2 and k >= 0, the T(n+1)-localised algebraic K-theory of BP<n>^{h p^k Z} (Z acting through Adams operations) is not K(n+1)-local, so the inclusion Sp_{K(n+1)} into Sp_{T(n+1)} is strict. The argument reduces this to the TC coassembly map not being an isomorphism for k >> 0, using cyclotomic redshift (Hahn-Wilson) and cyclotomic asymptotic constancy. The paper also reports failures of Galois hyperdescent, A^1-invariance and nil-invariance for K(n+1)-localised K-theory of K(n)-local E-infinity rings, and for n=1, p >= 7 it gives explicit computations of T(2)_*K(R) for certain finite Galois extensions R of the K(1)-local sphere (Section 7, which I could not read). Levy's MIT PhD thesis (May 2024) re-presents the height-2 argument and states that similar counterexamples exist for all n >= 2 and all primes; I treat that as the same result re-presented, not a new event.
events.delivers: A negative answer at every height n+1 >= 2 and every prime p: the conjectured equality of the K(n+1)-local and T(n+1)-local categories fails there (Theorem A, abstract). Restrictions: the non-K-locality is established for the specific rings BP<n>^{h p^k Z}, k >= 0, by a structural argument; explicit homotopy computations are given in the abstract/introduction only for n=1, p >= 7 (Section 7, not read by me). The abstract does not state the generalised or all-heights forms; those follow from Barthel's folklore equivalence (combined-heights conjecture iff generalised conjecture) and are my inference, not the paper's claim. Height 1 is not affected: the paper itself records that the height-1 case was already known (Mahowald at p=2, Miller at p>2).
events.remains: Nothing of problem_asks is left open at heights n >= 2: the equality is refuted at each such height and prime. Height 1 is positive (classical, 1981) and height 0 is trivial. What the judging pass must weigh is not a remaining gap in the statement but the status of the argument itself (single preprint, no journal acceptance found, Section 6 and Section 7 not read by me).

events.time_since_posted: about 35 months (as of 13 Oct 2026); no journal acceptance found
events.directly_checkable: The height-2 and n=1, p>=7 explicit computations in Section 7 are the directly checkable part of the argument; I could not read them. The general non-K-locality (Theorem A) is an argument, not a finite object anyone can check by hand.
events.direction: Against the conjecture: the paper asserts that the telescopic and chromatic localisations differ at every height n+1 >= 2 and every prime, so the conjectured equality is false at those heights. The height-1 instance is confirmed by classical results and is not contradicted.
events.object: The explicit rings BP<n>^{h p^k Z} for k >= 0 (fixed points of the Z-action by Adams operations on BP<n>). What is shown about them: their T(n+1)-localised algebraic K-theory is not K(n+1)-local, which makes the two localisations of spectra differ. The non-K-locality is deduced from structural inputs (TC coassembly map not an isomorphism for k >> 0, cyclotomic redshift), not from an explicit witness given in the abstract or introduction. Explicit homotopy computations are given only for n=1, p >= 7 (Section 7, unread by me).

events.what_happened: Shay Ben-Moshe, Shachar Carmeli, Tomer M. Schlank and Lior Yanovski, 'Descent and cyclotomic redshift for chromatically localized algebraic K-theory' (arXiv:2309.07123; v1 13 Sep 2023; v2 26 Nov 2024; journal reference Journal of the American Mathematical Society, DOI 10.1090/jams/1052). Proves that T(n+1)-localised algebraic K-theory satisfies descent for pi-finite p-group actions on categories of height up to n, that it sends T(n)-local Galois extensions to T(n+1)-local Galois extensions, and a cyclotomic redshift. The abstract states: 'Counterexamples to such cyclotomic hyperdescent for T(n+1)-localized K-theory were constructed by Burklund, Hahn, Levy and the third author, thereby disproving the telescope conjecture.'
events.revisions: v1 13 Sep 2023; v2 26 Nov 2024. Journal: JAMS, DOI 10.1090/jams/1052; the arXiv-page metadata says 2024 and a CRIS record I saw in search says vol. 38, issue 2 (2025). The two sources disagree on the year; I did not resolve it.
events.delivers: Redshift and descent results for chromatically localised algebraic K-theory. It does not by itself establish a failure of the telescope conjecture; its abstract attributes the counterexample to the BHLS paper. Combined with Levy's computations it gives the height-2 counterexample, per Levy's thesis abstract.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The paper says nothing about whether the K(n+1)-local and T(n+1)-local categories coincide; that question is handled by BHLS.

checked_by.who: Journal of the American Mathematical Society editors and referees
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the companion paper for publication (v2 Nov 2024, JAMS). This checks the redshift and descent results. It is not a check of the BHLS argument.

events.direction: Neutral on the conjecture by itself: it proves descent and redshift results for chromatically localised algebraic K-theory, which are inputs to the negative BHLS result.

events.what_happened: David Jongwon Lee and Ishan Levy, 'Topological Hochschild homology of the image of J' (arXiv:2307.04248; v1 9 Jul 2023; v2 31 Dec 2025). Computes mod (p,v1) and mod (2,eta,v1) THH of many variants of the image-of-J spectrum, including j_zeta; reports failure of Z_p Galois descent for THH along j_zeta to ell_p; proves the Segal conjecture for j_zeta at p > 2; computes K(L_{K(1)}S) in degrees up to 4p-6. The BHLS paper cites it for a THH constancy result and the Segal conjecture for these rings.
events.delivers: Computations of THH of image-of-J variants and a failure of Z_p Galois descent for THH. These are inputs to the K-theoretic route; they make no statement about the telescope conjecture.
events.direction: Not about the telescope conjecture: a THH and K-theory computation for K(1)-local-type rings. Discounted as a telescope result.

events.what_happened: Ishan Levy, 'The algebraic K-theory of the K(1)-local sphere via TC' (arXiv:2209.05314, submitted 12 Sep 2022, math.AT). Expresses the algebraic K-theory of the K(1)-local sphere and of the type-2 finite spectra through K-theory of discrete rings and TC of the connective ring j_zeta; gives an infinite family of 2-torsion classes in K_0 of type-2 spectra at p=2. Not a statement about the telescope conjecture. I took the date and abstract from search snippets and did not open the page.
events.delivers: K-theory computations for the K(1)-local sphere and type-2 spectra; no telescope statement.
events.direction: Not about the telescope conjecture; a precursor computation whose TC input is used in the BHLS height-2 route.

events.what_happened: David Lee (MIT) gave a talk at the SLMath Hot Topics workshop 'Life after the Telescope Conjecture' (9-13 Dec 2024), scheduled for 12 Dec 2024. The schedule abstract says it 'will disprove the telescope conjecture at height 2 and primes p > 5, by a direct computational approach', claiming that for k sufficiently large and Z acting by the Adams operation psi^{p+1}, V(2)_* TC(l^{h p^k Z}) has non-finite homotopy groups. I saw only the schedule abstract; no written version was found. The date is the talk date; the abstract itself is undated.
events.delivers: A claimed direct-computation route to a height-2 counterexample for p > 5 (abstract only). It overlaps the height-2 case already claimed in BHLS (which gives explicit computations for n=1, p >= 7). I could not check it.
events.remains: Nothing beyond the BHLS height-2 claim, which it appears to duplicate for p > 5.
events.time_since_posted: about 22 months since the scheduled talk
events.direction: Against the conjecture at height 2 for p > 5, if the abstract's claim holds. Unverified.
events.object: Claimed in the abstract only: for k >> 0 and Z acting via psi^{p+1}, V(2)_* TC(l^{h p^k Z}) has non-finite homotopy groups. No further detail was available.

events.what_happened: A talk 'THH of the image of J' at the University of Washington on 10 Mar 2026 (David Lee) described an ongoing project with Ishan Levy on v1-Bocksteins of THH groups of these rings. According to the event page's search snippet, it said the TC of these rings gives counterexamples to the telescope conjecture at height 2. I did not open the event page.
events.delivers: An ongoing project; no written result seen. Its telescope claim restates the height-2 counterexample already in BHLS.
events.direction: Consistent with the BHLS direction (against the conjecture at height 2); no new result.

events.what_happened: Douglas C. Ravenel, 'Cyclotomic extensions in stable homotopy theory' (arXiv:2606.08166; v1 6 Jun 2026; v2 12 Jul 2026; 75 pp.). Described in the abstract as an expository companion to his paper on cyclotomic spectra, aiming 'to shed light on the recent resolution of the telescope conjecture by Burklund, Hahn, Levy, and Schlank'. It compares higher cyclotomic extensions of commutative ring spectra with Galois extensions of p-adic fields. A table of contents with a section on the BHLS counterexample was seen only in a search-result mirror, not on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: An exposition of the BHLS disproof and of cyclotomic extensions. The abstract claims no new theorem about the telescope conjecture and gives no independent verification.

checked_by.qualification: Author of the conjecture and a leading chromatic homotopy theorist.
checked_by.what_they_did: Digested rewrite of the BHLS counterexample in an expository companion; whether he checked the argument is not stated in the abstract I read.

events.direction: Expository and consistent with the BHLS direction (negative).

events.what_happened: Jiacheng Liang (sole author), 'Generalized Telescope Conjecture' (arXiv:2609.03375; v1 3 Sep 2026; v2 5 Oct 2026; 119 pp.). Extends Balmer's tensor-triangular geometry through an 'atomic smashing frame' to arbitrary presentably symmetric monoidal infinity-categories and states a telescope conjecture in that generality. Proves recollement and descent results for it; embeds the smashing frame of Sp into a product over primes and heights of the smashing frames of the monochromatic layers Sp_{T(n)}; characterises the conjecture for infinity-topoi (via smashing fields) and for connective module categories (via Pierce-type conditions); introduces a Serre smashing frame.
events.revisions: v1 3 Sep 2026; v2 5 Oct 2026 (adds a dualisable internal-Hom formula for Artin gluing and a recollement principle for the telescope conjecture, per the arXiv comment).
events.delivers: A generalised formulation and structural results. The abstract says it does not prove or disprove Ravenel's telescope conjecture for Sp. The spatiality reduction to monochromatic layers concerns the smashing frame, not the equality at each height.
events.remains: Nothing in problem_asks. This is a different question (the generalised conjecture), recorded because it bears on the same name; the Sp-at-height-2-and-above question is already answered negatively by BHLS.
events.direction: Different question (the generalised telescope conjecture); no verdict on Ravenel's conjecture.

events.what_happened: Ravenel proposed (cited as [Rav92b]) that the conjecture should fail at chromatic heights 2 and above, and offered the parameterised Adams spectral sequence as a route to a counterexample. In his 2002 Manchester seminar abstract he wrote that he first stated the conjecture in 1977 and 'thought I had a disproof of it in the early 90s', and that 'the disproof has since fallen through'. I did not open the 2002 page; these statements come from search snippets.
events.delivers: Nothing established. A claimed disproof later withdrawn by its author.

withdrawn.what: Ravenel's early-1990s claimed disproof, via a parameterised Adams spectral sequence. The author describes it in 2002 as having 'fallen through'.
withdrawn.date: 2002 (author's own statement in a seminar abstract; the original claim is c. 1992)

events.direction: Would have cut against the conjecture; withdrawn, so it carries no weight.

events.what_happened: Mark Mahowald, Douglas Ravenel and Paul Shick, 'The triple loop space approach to the telescope conjecture', in Homotopy Methods in Algebraic Topology (ed. Greenlees, Contemp. Math. 271, AMS 2001, pp. 217-284; from a 1999 Boulder conference). Studies the Thom spectra y(n) and conjectures about their localised Adams spectral sequences which, if true, would give counterexamples at heights >= 2. Later surveys (search snippets only) say the approach did not produce a counterexample; Ravenel's 2017 talk has a slide titled 'The failed approach of MRS'. Hovey's page says 'Mahowald, Ravenel, and Shick have claimed to have a disproof for a long time'.
events.delivers: Conjectural; no established counterexample. Per a later survey (snippet), the height-1 check shows L_1 and the v_1-telescopic localisation of y(1) agree, so this route does not give a height-1 counterexample.
events.direction: Proposed a route that would have cut against the conjecture; not established.

events.what_happened: Agnès Beaudry, Mark Behrens, Prasit Bhattacharya, Dominic Culver and Zhouli Xu, 'The telescope conjecture at height 2 and the tmf resolution' (arXiv:1909.13379; v1 29 Sep 2019; v2 10 Jul 2021; published in the Journal of Topology, DOI 10.1112/topo.12208, per the arXiv page). Computes the tmf-resolution of a specific type-2 complex Z at p=2. The E1-page has a v2-periodic summand and a summand of bounded v2-torsion; the E2-page has unbounded v2-torsion. The telescope conjecture at height 2 at p=2 holds if this torsion dies in the spectral sequence and fails if it persists as v2-parabolas. The abstract does not settle which case occurs. Also proves a conjecture of Behrens and Egger that the E(2)-local ANSS for Z collapses.
events.revisions: v1 29 Sep 2019; v2 10 Jul 2021; journal version in J. Topology (2021), per the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Reduces the height-2, p=2 telescope question for the complex Z to a spectral-sequence question and does not decide it. Restricted to the specific complex Z at p=2.
events.remains: At height 2 and p=2 for this complex, the question is left open by this paper. BHLS claims all primes, including p=2, but I did not check the p=2 case in BHLS.

checked_by.who: Journal of Topology editors and referees
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2021), per the arXiv page; the journal version was not opened.

events.direction: Undecided, conditional: it describes what the telescope question at height 2 and p=2 depends on for this complex.

events.what_happened: Tobias Barthel, 'A short introduction to the telescope and chromatic splitting conjectures' (arXiv:1902.05046; v1 13 Feb 2019; v2 16 Feb 2019; 'accepted for publication in Surveys around Ohkawa's theorem on Bousfield classes'). Proves the folklore result that Ravenel's telescope conjecture for all heights combined is equivalent to the generalised telescope conjecture for the stable homotopy category. States Conjecture 3.4 (L_n^f -> L_n is an equivalence for n >= 0). Theorem 3.5 records the height-1 case as attributed to Bousfield, Mahowald and Miller.
events.revisions: v2 16 Feb 2019. The ar5iv rendering I read shows a header date of 9 Aug 2026, which does not match the arXiv listing; I did not resolve this and it does not change the event.
events.delivers: Expository. Establishes the equivalence of the all-heights and generalised forms, which is the link I use for the smashing-localisation form in problem_asks.
events.remains: Not applicable: an expository reformulation, not a resolution.

events.what_happened: Haynes Miller, 'On relations between Adams spectral sequences, with an application to the stable homotopy of a Moore space' (1981). Proves the height-1 telescope conjecture for odd primes, via the localised Adams spectral sequence for the mod p Moore spectrum with its v_1-self map (per Barthel's survey and the nLab summary). I did not read the 1981 paper.
events.delivers: The telescope conjecture holds at height 1 for odd primes: a restricted case (n=1, p odd).
events.remains: Heights n >= 2 at every prime; height 1 at p=2, which is Mahowald's result.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at height 1.

events.what_happened: Mark Mahowald's bo-resolutions (1981; with a further paper in 1982) prove the height-1 telescope conjecture at p=2, using the type-1 complex Y = M(2) smash C-eta (per the nLab summary and Barthel's survey). I did not read the original papers.
events.delivers: The telescope conjecture holds at height 1 for p=2: a restricted case (n=1, p=2).
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at height 1.

summary: The search found one event that settles the conjecture, and it is negative. Burklund, Hahn, Levy and Schlank posted arXiv:2310.17459 on 26 Oct 2023, three months before the frozen revision. The abstract, and Theorem A as I read it in the ar5iv rendering, say the telescopic and chromatic localisations of spectra differ at every prime p and every height n+1 >= 2, so Ravenel's conjectured equality fails at every height from 2 upward. Height 1 was already known (Miller 1981 for odd p; Mahowald 1981/82 for p=2), and height 0 is rationalisation. The all-heights and generalised forms follow from Barthel's folklore equivalence, which I read in his survey; the paper's abstract does not state them. The statement's phrase 'the last of Ravenel's conjectures to be resolved' is therefore satisfied in the negative. Expert engagement since then is substantial but not a line-by-line verification that I could find. Ausoni's Bourbaki exposé (Nov 2025) digests the disproof; Ravenel's own June 2026 companion (arXiv:2606.08166) explains the 'recent resolution'; an Oberwolfach workshop (Oct 2024) and an SLMath Hot Topics week (Dec 2024), both run by the authors, presented the ingredients; and the Clay Institute gave the four authors a Research Award on 14 Apr 2026 'in recognition of their remarkable construction of counterexamples'. Ben-Moshe, Carmeli, Schlank and Yanovski's cyclotomic redshift paper, which is an ingredient, was accepted by JAMS (v2 Nov 2024). I found no journal acceptance of the BHLS paper itself after about 35 months, and I did not find an erratum, a challenge or a withdrawal. In Quanta's August 2023 piece Michael Hopkins is quoted saying 'You couldn't touch a theorem like that' and Vesna Stojanoska says she had heard rumours; both are praise, not checks, and I have not counted them as checks. The Quanta snippet that the team explained the proof to about 200 mathematicians I could not confirm in the article text I opened, so I have not recorded it. Later work that uses the result: Levy's MIT thesis (May 2024; height-2 case and similar counterexamples for all n >= 2), Lee's 2024 and 2026 talks (direct computational routes at height 2, p > 5; ongoing project), and Liang's September 2026 preprint on a generalised telescope conjecture, which is a different question and proves no verdict on Sp. Pre-window history is in the record: Ravenel's early-1990s claimed disproof, which he withdrew in 2002; the 2001 Mahowald-Ravenel-Shick triple-loop-space programme, which did not yield a counterexample; and the 2019 Beaudry-Behrens-Bhattacharya-Culver-Xu height-2 p=2 tmf-resolution paper, which reduces the question to a spectral-sequence dichotomy without deciding it. On AI: I ran several searches explicitly for AI involvement (AI-model proof, LLM/GPT/Gemini/Claude, AlphaEvolve/AlphaProof, AI-assisted chromatic homotopy in 2026, Lean formalisation) and found nothing naming an AI system for this problem. The AlphaEvolve 67-problem paper (arXiv:2511.02864) has no telescope mention in the portion I could read. I read only parts of the BHLS paper (abstract, introduction, Sections 1-2.4 and 3.1 in the renderings), so the 'none found' finding rests on the sources read, including the acknowledgements fragment I saw, which names mathematicians and funders and no tool.
competing_reading: The strongest case against counting this as a settled resolution is that it rests on a single 100-page preprint with no journal acceptance found after about 35 months and no published referee report or erratum. Its key steps (the Section 6 argument and the explicit Section 7 computations) were not read by me, so the public record is mostly expository: the authors' own workshops, an expert's Bourbaki digest, and the conjecture author's companion. On that reading the problem is settled by reputation rather than by a checked written argument. Against this: the expository record is unusually deep (Bourbaki, Ravenel's companion, two workshops, a JAMS-accepted companion for a key ingredient), the Clay Institute has recognised the work, and no one has challenged it. A second reading concerns scope. The conjecture is refuted at heights >= 2, while height 0 and height 1 were settled positively in 1981 and at height 0 trivially; so the question is answered in every height, but the answer is positive at heights 0-1 and negative at heights >= 2, and a reader who wants a single verdict on 'the telescope conjecture' has to decide which parts count. A third reading concerns the frozen January 2024 wording, which lists the problem as open although the BHLS preprint was public three months earlier; that is a fact about the list for the judging pass, not something I have resolved.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A full read of arXiv:2310.17459, in particular Section 6 (the disproof argument), Section 7 (the explicit n=1, p>=7 computations) and the complete acknowledgements, to confirm the scope claimed in the abstract and to check for any computer or AI assistance. (2) A journal acceptance record or referee report for arXiv:2310.17459, or a published erratum. (3) The full text of Ausoni's Bourbaki exposé (Exp. 1242), to see whether it states that the argument was checked. (4) Ravenel's 2026 companion read in full, for whether it reports checking the BHLS argument. (5) The Schlank ICM 2026 survey, hosted on Ravenel's site, which I could not parse and which may carry the authors' own status statement. (6) A formal-conjectures or mathlib entry for the telescope conjecture, with its status tag, to rule out a machine-checked or disproof-tagged record.

dead_ends: No AI system named in any source about this conjecture: 40 WebSearch queries and fetches of the relevant papers found none. The AlphaEvolve 67-problem paper (arXiv:2511.02864) has no telescope mention in the portion I could read.
No Lean or mathlib formalisation found. The formal-conjectures repository was searched, not browsed, so its telescope entry (if any) is unchecked.
No Notices or Bulletin article on the disproof found.
No journal acceptance of 2310.17459 found in search results or arXiv metadata.
Quanta's claim (from a search snippet) that the team explained the proof to about 200 mathematicians could not be confirmed in the article text I opened; not recorded.

Shai Keidar's Galois-descent reformulation (Oberwolfach 2024 talk) has no written version found; his arXiv 2412.07716 is about the telescopic Picard group and does not mention the telescope conjecture.
Mark Hovey's 1999 memoir with Strickland (Morava K-theories and localisation) is background only; no link to the disproof found.
Balchin and Stevenson 'Big categories, big spectra' appeared in a search summary as a framework for the finite-versus-smashing question; I did not open it and it predates the counterexamples.

Land-Mathew-Meier-Tamme purity (height-1 finite localisation of K-theory, 2024) appeared in search results; it is about K-theory localisation, not the telescope conjecture itself, and I did not open it.
A 2026 survey described by a search summary as 'Stable homotopy theory of higher categories' (arXiv 2605.05195) appeared in results; its snippet was unreadable and I did not open it.
